text: On-prem SQL Server means you own the whole stack — hardware, OS patching, SQL Server patching, storage, backups, HA/DR. Azure SQL is Microsoft's umbrella term for options that each move a different slice of that ownership onto Microsoft instead.

On a traditional on-prem server, you own everything above the concrete floor — hardware, the OS, SQL Server itself, networking, backups, and the pager at 2 a.m. when any layer fails. Total ownership, total responsibility.
The real shift isn't "the same server, somewhere else" — it's which responsibilities move to Microsoft and which stay with you, and that split differs across the three deployment options.
Understanding that there's a trade, and what's being traded, is what makes the next comparison make sense. Next up: the three concrete options this umbrella covers, side by side.
